previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on hemodialysis via a right femoral tunneled catheter and advanced HIV/AIDS on HAART presented with progressive right leg swelling and pain shortly after catheter placement. Lower-extremity ultrasound showed no DVT, and CT pelvis demonstrated marked edema but limited assessment for thrombus around the catheter because it occupied most of the right external iliac vein; she was treated for presumed catheter-associated DVT with a heparin infusion bridged to warfarin until therapeutic INR, with swelling resolving after in-hospital dialysis and by discharge. During the admission she developed right-eye conjunctivitis with periorbital swelling and morning purulence; Ophthalmology started polymyxin/bacitracin ointment and a 7-day course of valacyclovir given prior herpes ophthalmicus, and HSV/VZV testing from a lesion was negative with near-complete symptom resolution. Chest discomfort and odynophagia were felt most consistent with esophagitis and resolved after completing a 14-day fluconazole course. She continued scheduled hemodialysis, EPO for anemia of CKD, and HIV therapy with opportunistic infection prophylaxis, and was discharged home with services, warfarin with INR monitoring arranged through dialysis, and completion of eye medications.
problems: Presumed catheter-associated deep venous thrombosis/right lower extremity edema treated with heparin bridge to warfarin
End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via right femoral tunneled catheter; dialysis access complication

Advanced HIV/AIDS on HAART with opportunistic infection prophylaxis
Chest discomfort/odynophagia felt due to esophagitis; completed fluconazole
Anemia of chronic kidney disease treated with EPO during hemodialysis
Secondary hyperparathyroidism; cinacalcet dose reduced and phosphate binder continued
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (history; anticoagulation addressed with warfarin for presumed DVT)
Hyperkalemia on admission without EKG changes, improved with dialysis

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ female with left great toe in plantar aspect of foot
pain.  Question fracture.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

AP, lateral and oblique views of the left foot.  The bones are osteopenic
without focal area of osteolysis.  There is no acute fracture.  Degenerative
changes are noted at the joint between the navicular and medial cuneiform. 
Atherosclerotic calcifications noted in the small vessels.

IMPRESSION:

No acute fracture.

HISTORY:  ___ female with end-stage renal disease, tunnel dialysis
catheter cuff has been pulled out of the skin.  Replacement required.  

COMPARISON:  Chest x-ray ___ 

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___, supervising and present throughout
the procedure, Dr. ___ fellow).

ANESTHESIA:   Local anesthesia with 1% lidocaine was given around the right
femoral vein tunnel site.

FLUOROSCOPY:  Total fluoro time 1 min 15 s, 13 mGy.   No IV contrast used.  

PROCEDURE:  Tunneled dialysis catheter replacement over a wire. 

PROCEDURE IN DETAIL :

An informed written consent was obtained after explaining the procedure,
benefits, alternatives and risks involved.  The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The right groin and
tunneled line were prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A
preprocedure time out was performed per ___ protocol. 

Under fluoroscopy, the tip of the old catheter was at the cavoatrial junction.
Both lumens were aspirated prior to removing the tunneled catheter over an
Amplatz wire.  Once the catheter was removed, a peel-away sheath was placed,
through which a new 55 cm tip to cuff hemodialysis catheter was inserted.  The
sheath was then peeled away.  The tip of the catheter was positioned in the
right atrium, and the Amplatz wire was removed.  

Both ports aspirated and flushed easily.  Each was flushed with saline and
capped.  The catheter was secured to the skin using 0 silk sutures, and a
sterile dressing was applied. 

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.  

FINDINGS:

Tip of the catheter in the right atrium.  

IMPRESSION:

Uncomplicated over the wire exchange of right femoral vein tunneled dialysis
catheter.
